comment: Multi-jurisdiction routing layer. Three things this models: (a) what each tribunal applies as its default rule of decision (the 'governing law' question — ADGM applies English law wholesale; DIFC applies its own RDC + Damages Law; SICC applies Singapore law unless parties choose otherwise); (b) which rule modules act as 'recognition gates' for foreign judgments / arbitral awards (the NY Convention path); and (c) which rule modules carry a public-policy override (the last-resort refusal of enforcement). The conflict-of-laws resolver in /api/conflict_route consumes this file alongside _claims.json.

tribunals.label: DIFC Courts (incl. Digital Economy Court)
tribunals.default_governing_law: DIFC own statutes (RDC, DIFC Damages Law, DIFC Contract Law) + UAE Federal Law
tribunals.recognition_path: DIFC Courts Law Articles 15(1), 24(D); DIFC Damages Law Article 36; RDC 25.1(10), 28.51-52; common-law Norwich Pharmacal + Bankers Trust
tribunals.public_policy_authority: DIFC public policy; UAE federal public policy as subsidiary

tribunals.label: ADGM Courts
tribunals.default_governing_law: English common law via the Application of English Law Regulations 2015
tribunals.recognition_path: ADGM Arbitration Regulations 2015 (parallels SG IAA s 31)
tribunals.public_policy_authority: ADGM public policy under s 56(3)(b) of the Arbitration Regulations

tribunals.label: Singapore International Commercial Court
tribunals.default_governing_law: Singapore law (or parties' chosen law per IAA / Choice of Court Act)
tribunals.recognition_path: International Arbitration Act s 31 (NY Convention Article V)
tribunals.public_policy_authority: Singapore public policy under s 31(4)(b) IAA

rule_jurisdictions.applied_via: UAE federal law as subsidiary to ADGM/DIFC zone law

cross_border_paths.name: Foreign arbitral award → DIFC seat
cross_border_paths.note: DIFC's recognition path for foreign arbitral awards routes through the New York Convention (the UAE is a signatory). Substantive challenges go through DIFC Damages Law / DIFC Courts Law; ancillary disclosure and tracing orders use Norwich Pharmacal + Bankers Trust + RDC 28.52 (the trace-07 path).

cross_border_paths.name: Foreign arbitral award → ADGM seat
cross_border_paths.note: ADGM Arbitration Regulations 2015 s 56 parallels SG IAA s 31 and NY Convention Article V; same conjunctive-grounds shape. Substantive contract layer applies English common law via the AELR.

cross_border_paths.name: Foreign arbitral award → SICC seat
cross_border_paths.note: Singapore IAA s 31 is the canonical NY Convention implementation; trace-06 reproduces it on a US-seated FA. DKT v DKU four-condition framework supplies the natural-justice sub-gate.

cross_border_paths.name: Cross-tribunal contract dispute (ADGM ↔ DIFC)
cross_border_paths.note: ADGM applies English law wholesale; DIFC applies its own statutes plus UAE federal law as subsidiary. A contract subject to ADGM law sued in DIFC will see English contract interpretation principles applied through the lens of DIFC's Conflict of Laws Law, with UAE Art 390 LD-cap available as a federal overlay.

cross_border_paths.name: Stablecoin reserves tracing — Hong Kong primary, DIFC ancillary
cross_border_paths.note: The trace-07 pattern (Techteryx v IG): primary fraud action in HK; DIFC issues WFO + disclosure orders against UAE-domiciled assets and accounts at international trading platforms. Cross-border recognition is achieved via DIFC's interim-relief jurisdiction (Articles 15(1), 24(D) of the Courts Law) rather than NY Convention.
